answer: A bond-priced identity is the cheapest Sybil defence: each agent posts a stake sized to the median epoch reward, escrowed and slashed on attested misbehaviour. Faking a mesa of independent voices therefore costs one funded stake per puppet, so ten thousand identities freeze ten thousand deposits at risk at once. Work comes from a rotating roster and history is scored on one shared field of evidence, so a fresh violet account inherits no weighting. To forge diversity this way, the attacker pays linearly while reward grows slower, so the attack turns cash-negative before quorum.
